script.base: Spread and total are not in the pack, so the script is inferred from form only: a competitive, role-stable game, not a declared shootout or blowout. Both clubs already run through one back (Skattebo 50 carries/177 yards, Love 41/160) and both fronts have been soft (NYG 4.94 YPC allowed, ARI 4.63). Neither blitzes heavily (NYG 26%, ARI 22%), so the base flow is NYG feeding Skattebo and ARI mixing Love with McBride as the first read (34 targets, 211 yards, 182 air yards).
script.flip1: NYG falls behind and abandons the run. Skattebo's 16.7-carry pace dies the way a trailing back's line dies, and NYG's QB is already -0.62 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=29) against +0.28 clean, so even ARI's 22% blitz rate can turn the comeback into failed deep shots (Nabers 185 air yards for 96 rec yards, Fields 213 air for 74).
script.flip2: ARI gets up and hands it to Love, or pressure (ARI QB -0.12 EPA vs blitz, n=28, vs +0.18 clean) turns the game into a short-yardage slog. McBride's 11.3 targets shrink, Wilson's 295 air yards never become explosives against a NYG defense that has allowed only 6 passes of 20+ on 101 attempts, and both overs die together.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Skattebo is the NYG bellcow at 50 carries and 177 rush yards over 3 games, well clear of Harris (13) and Singletary (9), and ARI has allowed 4.63 YPC plus 11 runs of 10+, so a normal 16-carry day only needs a small efficiency bump to clear 62.5, which is just 3.5 yards above his 59-yard average.
edge_players.must_be_true: He is active with no snap cap (not in the pack), keeps about 15 or more carries, and NYG is not forced to abandon the run.
edge_players.kills_it: NYG trails and goes pass-only, or Harris and Singletary cut him to about 12 carries at his own 3.54 YPC, which stays under 62.5.

edge_players.edge_sentence: McBride is ARI's primary receiver by a clear margin (34 targets, 211 yards, 182 air yards in 3 games, about 70 yards a game) and 63.5 sits under that role, while NYG has barely been attacked in the middle (9 attempts, 8.11 YPA) where the TE lives.
edge_players.must_be_true: He plays his normal snaps and stays the first read, and ARI does not spend the afternoon in a Love clock-grind that cuts pass attempts.
edge_players.kills_it: ARI leads early and runs — Love already has 41 carries and 160 yards — or NYG brackets the TE and the 34-target role does not travel.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost because the missing spread was a blowout the form could not see. NYG trailed, Skattebo's 50-carry role shrank, and his 3.54 YPC never rose to ARI's 4.63 allowed, so 12 carries finished near 42 while Harris (4.46 YPC on 13 carries) took the efficient runs. ARI saw NYG allow 4.94 YPC, handed the game to Love (41 carries, 160 yards), and McBride's 11-target pace became 6 targets in the mid-40s, under 63.5. That counter-case is serious and is why both are leans, not strong, but it is not stronger than the role reads unless the real spread shows a big favorite.
slip_story: One competitive-game stack, not a shootout and not a clock-kill: Skattebo rush over (NYG runs on ARI's soft front) with McBride rec over (ARI's first read, line under his rate). They win together only if neither team blows the other out. Do not add Wilson (54.3 yards, 295 air yards, into a defense with 6 explosives on 101 throws), Nabers over 55 (32-yard role), Love over 66.5 (13 yards above his 53-yard rate), or any TD.
